After completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed before the Court below for the offences under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471 and 120B IPC and Sections 3, 4, 5 & 6 of Prize Chits & Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act, 1978.

sentences.text: 3. As per the prosecution case, the accused petitioners are the designated partners/Directors of Apexa Associates LLP, Apexa Rise Project LLP, Apexa Rise Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd., Apexa Rise Investment and Apexa Infra.

entities.text: Apexa Rise Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: and they induced people to invest their money into the business of these companies/firms and in good faith, people invested their hard-earned money in the business.

It is alleged that the accused petitioners misappropriated the business money and purchased several movable and immovable properties in their/their family members' name and as a result of which the business suffered a huge financial loss.
It is also alleged that the accused petitioners thus, played fraud upon the investors who invested their hard earned money into their business in good faith.
4. Learned counsels for the accused petitioners submit that the petitioners have falsely been implicated in this case.
It is argued by them that the alleged offences are triable by magistrate and after completion of investigation, police has filed charge-sheet in the matter before the learned court below.
They further submit that now nothing is to be investigated or recovered from their instance.
They further submit that trial will take considerable time in its conclusion.
They thus, submit that no fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the petitioners behind the bars for indefinite time period.

5. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor as well as learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail applications and submit that the petitioners have played fraud upon the investors and misappropriated the business funds.
It is further contended that the petitioners are habitual offender and have previous criminal antecedents.
They thus, sought dismissal of the bail applications.

sentences.text: I have considered the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioners as well as learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant and perused the material available on record.

9. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, more particularly the fact that the alleged offences are triable by magistrate and after completion of investigation, chargesheet has been filed before the court below and trial will take considerable time in its conclusion, I deem it just and proper to allow the bail applications under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
(8 of 8) [CRLMB-331/2023]
10.

These bail applications are accordingly, allowed and it is directed that accused-petitioners shall be released on bail provided each of them furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lac Only) together with two sureties in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court with the stipulation that each of them shall appear before that Court and any court to which the matter is transferred, on all subsequent dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
11.
However, it is made clear that the petitioners shall not involve in similar offence(s) during pendency of bail granted by this Court.
The petitioners are further directed to mark their presence in the concerned police station on first Monday of every month, till trial is concluded.
If breach of any of these conditions is reported or come to the notice of the Court, the same shall alone be a reason for the trial court to cancel the bail granted to them by this Court.
12. A copy of this order may be placed in each file.
